relationships.subject: TNF-α
relationships.evidence_quote: Direct incision evidence now includes antisense and pharmacologic studies linking TNF-α/p38/NF-κB signaling to NaV1.8 and NaV1.9 expression and acute hypersensitivity

relationships.subject: thrombospondin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: The same study identified immune-cell-derived thrombospondin-1 as an inhibitor of nociceptor sensitization

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Selective NaV1.8 inhibition validates peripheral channel tractability for acute pain but not prevention of CPSP.

key_findings: Review: incision-triggered TNF-α/p38/NF-κB signaling is linked to NaV1.8/NaV1.9 expression and acute hypersensitivity, but no human study shows the full immune-to-channel-to-persistent-pain sequence.
Selective NaV1.8 inhibition gives acute analgesia but is not shown to prevent chronic postsurgical pain.
